original_interpretation: SEMI MMDS reports materials revenue for seven regions (North America, Europe, Japan, Taiwan, South Korea, China, Rest of World) and publishes detailed history only for silicon shipments, photoresist, photoresist ancillaries, process gases and lead frames.
evidence_found: "reports revenue for seven market regions (North America, Europe, Japan, Taiwan, South Korea, China and Rest of World). The report also features detailed historical data for silicon shipments and revenues for photoresist, photoresist ancillaries, process gases and lead frames." (SEMI release, May 12, 2026 (semi.org; same text on PR Newswire 302768700), MMDS boilerplate paragraph)
correction: Source lists these as the detailed historical series the report 'features'; it does not say these are the only detailed series ('only' is the researcher's addition).
notes: SEMI describing its own subscription product: closer to reported_claim than fact. Same boilerplate appears in the 2022-2024 releases.

original_interpretation: SEMI said lithography-related materials (photomask, photoresist and ancillaries) and wet chemicals had strong double-digit growth in 2025.
evidence_found: "Lithography-related materials, including photomask, photoresist and ancillaries, along with wet chemicals, posted strong double-digit growth as higher process intensity and tighter lithography requirements continued to increase materials consumption." (SEMI release, May 12, 2026 (semi.org; same text on PR Newswire 302768700), para 2)
notes: Segment growth rates themselves are not published; qualitative only.

original_interpretation: SEMI said substrates and bonding wire led 2025 packaging materials growth, helped by higher gold prices in bonding wire.
evidence_found: "Packaging materials revenue grew 9.3% to $27.4 billion in 2025. Substrates and bonding wire led the increase, supported by higher gold prices in bonding wire and stronger demand for advanced substrates." (SEMI release, May 12, 2026 (semi.org; same text on PR Newswire 302768700), para 3)

original_interpretation: SEMI put China's 2025 semiconductor materials consumption at US$15.6 billion (second) and South Korea's at US$11.2 billion (third).
evidence_found: "China ranked second at $15.6 billion, supported by double-digit growth, followed by South Korea at $11.2 billion." (SEMI release, May 12, 2026 (semi.org; same text on PR Newswire 302768700), para 4); regional table image (US$ bn, MMDS May 2026): China $15.6 (+12.5%), South Korea $11.2 (+2.4%).
notes: Ship-to consumption, not production. Table image on PR Newswire copy also confirms the values.

original_interpretation: SIA/BCG (2021) say many suppliers of key materials (silicon wafers, photoresist, other specialty chemicals) are concentrated in China and East Asia, alongside about 75% of manufacturing capacity.
evidence_found: "About 75% of semiconductor manufacturing capacity, as well as many suppliers of key materials—such as silicon wafers, photoresist, and other specialty chemicals—are concentrated in China and East Asia, a region significantly exposed to high seismic activity and geopolitical tensions." (SIA/BCG Apr 2021, executive summary)
notes: 2021 report; the 75% capacity share is as of c.2020 and may be dated. Joint SIA/BCG analysis: industry_body source type acceptable, though content is consultant analysis.

original_interpretation: SIA/BCG (2024) put front-end materials at US$40bn of a US$64bn materials market, with silicon wafers and photoresist about half of front-end (US$19.5bn).
evidence_found: "The $64 billion semiconductor materials market comprises chemicals and materials used in the front-end ($40 billion) and back-end (ATP) ($24 billion) of the supply chain. Silicon wafers and photoresist comprise about half of the total market for front-end materials ($19.5 billion)" (SIA/BCG May 2024, 'Materials' section; Exhibit 11 source: SEMI; IHS; BCG analysis)
notes: Base year of the market sizes is not stated in the passage; metric period 'not stated (c. 2022)' is appropriately hedged.

original_interpretation: SIA/BCG (2024) say most leading materials companies are headquartered in Japan, the US and the EU, and Japan has at least three of the leading vendors in multiple segments.
evidence_found: "Most leading materials companies are headquartered in Japan, the United States, and the EU (see Exhibit 11). There are multiple segments of the front-end and back-end materials market where Japan is home to at least three of the leading vendors." (SIA/BCG May 2024, 'Materials' section)

original_interpretation: SIA/BCG (2024) say low-volume, high-value materials such as EUV photoresist tend to stay near suppliers' main bases (IP and quality risk), while commodity resists, purified HF and bulk gases are co-located near fabs.
evidence_found: "Producers of low-volume, high-value, technically advanced materials, such as extreme ultra-violet (EUV) photoresist, weigh the risk of IP leakage and the difficulty of ensuring efficient, high-quality production far from their main production bases. ... materials for which production knowledge is widely dispersed ... have a greater incentive to be co-located near fabs. Examples include older generations of photoresist, purified straight chemicals such as hydrofluoric acid, and bulk gases" (SIA/BCG May 2024, Materials)
correction: The report describes incentives ('weigh the risk', 'have a greater incentive to be co-located'), not an observed location pattern; 'commodity resists' is the report's 'older generations of photoresist'. Reword as: SIA/BCG say EUV-resist makers weigh IP-leakage and quality risks of producing far from home bases, while older-generation resists, purified HF and bulk gases have a greater incentive to be co-located near fabs.

original_interpretation: A December 2023 BIS survey cited by SIA/BCG found industry concern about domestic US sources of bare wafers, gases and wet chemicals.
evidence_found: "A survey published in December 2023 by BIS found that industry respondents “expressed significant concern about domestic sources of three categories of materials: bare wafers, gases, and wet chemicals.”" (SIA/BCG May 2024, Materials, footnote 20)
notes: Secondary citation of a BIS (US Commerce) survey; the BIS original was not opened, so this verifies what SIA/BCG report BIS found.

original_interpretation: SIA/BCG (2024) list materials localisation investments: Hemlock polysilicon (>US$370m, Michigan), Entegris Colorado Springs (US$600m), GlobalWafers 300 mm wafers (Texas), Dongwoo Fine Chem photoresist (Iksan) and Entegris wet chemicals and CMP slurries (US$500m, Kaohsiung).
evidence_found: "Hemlock Semiconductor ... invested more than $370 million to expand its facilities in Michigan; Entegris ... is undertaking a $600 million expansion of its center of excellence in Colorado Springs; Global Wafers is building a new 300 mm silicon wafer plant in Texas ... Dongwoo Fine Chem announced a new photoresist line at its Iksan plant ... Entegris is building a $500 million wet chemicals and CMP slurries plant in Kaohsiung" (SIA/BCG May 2024, Materials)
notes: Status as of May 2024; the list also includes Calumet's 60,000 sq ft substrates facility in Michigan (omitted by the claim). Project status since then not checked.

original_interpretation: SIA/BCG (2024) say gallium, rare earths and many other critical minerals are still largely sourced from single regions, with most mining and refining in mainland China.
evidence_found: "certain raw materials, including gallium, rare earths, and many other critical minerals, are still largely sourced from single regions. There are efforts to source some of these critical materials by recycling from old devices, but the vast majority of mining and refining for these materials is done in Mainland China." (SIA/BCG May 2024, Materials, fn 22)

original_interpretation: SEMI estimated global semiconductor materials revenue at US$67.5 billion in 2024 (as first reported).
evidence_found: "Global semiconductor materials market revenue increased 3.8% to $67.5 billion in 2024" (SEMI release Apr 28, 2025, para 1; table total $67,468m)
notes: As first reported. The May 2026 release ('increased 6.8% year-over-year to $73.2 billion in 2025') implies a restated 2024 base of about US$68.5bn (73.2/1.068); not published explicitly.

original_interpretation: SEMI estimated wafer fabrication materials revenue at US$42.9 billion in 2024.
evidence_found: "Wafer fabrication materials revenue increased 3.3% to $42.9 billion in 2024, while packaging materials revenue grew 4.7% to $24.6 billion last year." (SEMI release Apr 28, 2025, para 2)
notes: First-reported figure. May 2026 release ('Wafer fabrication materials revenue increased 5.4% to $45.8 billion') implies a restated 2024 base of about US$43.5bn; label as 'as first reported'.

original_interpretation: SEMI estimated packaging materials revenue at US$24.6 billion in 2024.
evidence_found: "packaging materials revenue grew 4.7% to $24.6 billion last year." (SEMI release Apr 28, 2025, para 2)
notes: First-reported figure. May 2026 release ('Packaging materials revenue grew 9.3% to $27.4 billion in 2025') implies a restated 2024 base of about US$25.1bn; label as 'as first reported'.

original_interpretation: SEMI reported silicon (wafer) materials revenue fell 7.1% in 2024, the only segment besides SOI that did not grow, while CMP, photoresist and ancillaries grew by strong double digits.
evidence_found: "The chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), photoresist, and photoresist ancillaries segments experienced strong double-digit growth ... All semiconductor materials segments, except for silicon and silicon-on-insulator (SOI), registered year-on-year increases. ... resulting in a 7.1% decline in silicon revenue in 2024." (SEMI Apr 28, 2025, para 2)
notes: SOI's own 2024 change is not published. 'silicon (wafer)' is the researcher's gloss of SEMI's 'silicon' segment.

original_interpretation: SEMI put 2024 materials consumption at US$20.1bn in Taiwan (15th year as largest), US$13.5bn in China and US$10.5bn in Korea; Japan was the only region to decline.
evidence_found: "Taiwan, with $20.1 billion in revenue, was the world's largest consumer of semiconductor materials for the 15th consecutive year. China, at $13.5 billion ... ranking second in 2024, while Korea followed as the third largest consumer with $10.5 billion in revenue. All regions, except for Japan, posted single-digit increases in 2024." (SEMI Apr 28, 2025, para 3; table: Taiwan $20,090m, China $13,458m, South Korea $10,451m, Japan -3.2%)
notes: First-reported 2024 values; May 2026 YoY rates imply slightly restated 2024 bases (Taiwan ~US$20.0bn, China ~US$13.9bn, Korea ~US$10.9bn), not published explicitly.

original_interpretation: In SEMI's regional materials data, 'Rest of World' covers Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines, other Southeast Asia and smaller markets.
evidence_found: "Note: Summed subtotals may not equal the total due to rounding. Rest of the World includes Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines, other areas of Southeast Asia, and smaller global markets." (SEMI release May 6, 2024 (PR Newswire copy), note under regional table)
notes: Same definition repeated in the 2022, 2024 and 2025 release tables.

original_interpretation: SEMI estimated global semiconductor materials revenue at US$66.7 billion in 2023 (as first reported).
evidence_found: "Global semiconductor materials market revenue in 2023 contracted 8.2% to $66.7 billion from the market record of $72.7 billion set in 2022" (SEMI release May 6, 2024 (PR Newswire copy), para 1; table total $66,721m)
notes: Correctly labelled 'as first reported'. SEMI's April 2025 release table restates 2023 total to $64,994m (see new claim @r_tot23).

original_interpretation: SEMI estimated wafer fabrication materials revenue at US$41.5 billion in 2023.
evidence_found: "Wafer fabrication materials revenue declined 7.0% to $41.5 billion in 2023, while packaging materials revenue fell 10.1% to $25.2 billion last year." (SEMI release May 6, 2024 (PR Newswire copy), para 2)
notes: The April 2025 release growth rate (42.9/1.033 = 41.5) implies the 2023 wafer fab figure was not materially restated; the restatement fell on packaging.

original_interpretation: SEMI estimated packaging materials revenue at US$25.2 billion in 2023.
evidence_found: "packaging materials revenue fell 10.1% to $25.2 billion last year." (SEMI release May 6, 2024 (PR Newswire copy), para 2). Newer: "packaging materials revenue grew 4.7% to $24.6 billion last year" (SEMI Apr 28, 2025) implies a 2023 base of ~US$23.5bn; restated 2023 total $64,994m (Apr 2025 table).
correction: US$25.2bn is the May 2024 first-reported value. SEMI's April 2025 data imply 2023 packaging materials of about US$23.5bn (24.6/1.047), consistent with the restated 2023 total of US$64,994m. See superseding inference @r_pkg23.

original_interpretation: SEMI said silicon, photoresist ancillaries, wet chemicals and CMP had the largest 2023 contractions in fab materials, and organic substrates drove most of the packaging decline.
evidence_found: "The silicon, photoresist ancillaries, wet chemicals, and chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) segments logged the biggest contractions in the wafer fabrication materials market. The organic substrates segment accounted for much of the packaging materials market contraction." (SEMI release May 6, 2024 (PR Newswire copy), para 2)

original_interpretation: SEMI attributed the 2023 materials decline to inventory reduction that lowered fab utilisation and materials consumption.
evidence_found: "Demand for semiconductors softened in 2023 as the industry worked to reduce excess inventory, leading to lower fab utilization rates and, consequently, a drop in materials consumption." (SEMI release May 6, 2024 (PR Newswire copy), para 3)
notes: SEMI's causal attribution; correctly framed as 'SEMI attributed'.

original_interpretation: China was the only region whose semiconductor materials consumption grew in 2023 (+0.9%), while South Korea fell 18.0%.

Table: "China $13,085 $12,970 0.9 %"; "South Korea $10,575 $12,901 -18.0 %" (SEMI release May 6, 2024 (PR Newswire copy)). SEMI later restated China's 2023 figure to US$12,779m, below the first-reported 2022 value of US$12,970m; restated 2022 values were not found in any public release opened, so whether China still grew in 2023 on restated data is unknown.
